The register values do not themselves gate or block a transfer, so the RTL does not show an availability mechanism. No privileged mode, test, bypass or similar integration behavior is shown acting directly on the stored values.",

conceptual assets.information: The writable architectural register values held in reg_file provide operands to the surrounding execution datapath and can contain application data.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Confidentiality is at risk because register contents can contain application data and are returned through rs1_o, rs2_o and rs3_o at lines 88-89, 126-127 and 141. Integrity is at risk because rd_i can modify the stored values on clocked assignments at lines 86 and 110. The register values do not themselves gate or block a transfer, so the RTL does not show an availability mechanism. No privileged mode, test, bypass or similar integration behavior is shown acting directly on the stored values.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could observe operand outputs or obtain an unauthorized write operation through rd_i and the control inputs to disclose or corrupt architectural register values.

conceptual assets.information: The decision governing whether a write targeting register zero is suppressed preserves the fixed-zero register behavior on which processor execution depends; it is generated inside the unit and has no entry or exit port.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because rd_zero compares the write address with zero and contributes to the write-permission decision rf_we at lines 76-77, while the ASIC implementation fixes reg_file(0) to zero at line 117. Undermined expected behavior is at risk because rf_zero_we overrides the suppression decision and forces the target address to zero at lines 77-80, so changing that override can violate the fixed-zero behavior.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could bypass the zero-register write protection or force the zero-write override so that register zero changes and subsequent execution becomes incorrect.

considered, not kept.concept: Register access commands and operand selectors
considered, not kept.reason: The register addresses, read/write enables and operand selection fields only specify which register access occurs, so Access command fields treats them as part of the access rather than as separate information of their own (lines 76-80, 109, 126-127, 141 and 144).

RST_EN, RVE_EN and RS3_EN only select implementation structure, register-file size or the presence of the third read port at build time and cannot be changed or withheld at run time (lines 31-35, 68-69, 98-99 and 136-149).
The clock and reset only time or reset register-file and output assignments, and the Clocks and resets rule excludes them as conceptual assets (lines 84-90, 104-112 and 120-128).
